environment.description: Same NestJS microservice on ECS Fargate. PostgreSQL 15 RDS with connection routed through PgBouncer (transaction mode). The database role 'webhook_ro_proc' is configured with a pg_hba.conf entry restricting connections from the application CIDR only. Role privileges: the role inherits from a base role 'readonly_base' which has SELECT granted on specific tables via column-level grants (employees.id, employees.name, employees.department only - webhook_response column excluded from SELECT grant). No INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on any table. Additionally, a row-level security policy on employees table restricts visibility to department = current_setting('app.department'). The RDS instance has IAM authentication enabled but the application uses md5 password auth through PgBouncer's auth_query mechanism. Note: the SSRF vulnerability in the callback URL fetch remains exploitable for reading internal network resources - the database restriction only prevents persistence/exfiltration via stored results.

config.database_grants: GRANT SELECT (id, name, department) ON employees TO readonly_base; GRANT readonly_base TO webhook_ro_proc; NO INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE grants; RLS enabled
config.network: Private subnet with NAT, no egress filtering on port 80/443
config.imds: IMDSv2 required (token-based, but axios single GET still works for token endpoint)
config.rls_policy: CREATE POLICY dept_isolation ON employees USING (department = current_setting('app.department'))
